The Niigata Field Share · a one year share of a rice terrace

Grow your ownJapan.

In parts of London you can wait 15 years for an allotment. In Niigata, a rice terrace is ready for you next June. You do not move there: a local farmer tends it all year, and you come for a weekend to plant it in June, to harvest it in October, or both. In February it comes home as sake, poured into a copper cup you made yourself.

How Europe will notice

Europe queues for soil. Niigata's terraces need hands.

Across England and Germany, people wait years for a small garden plot. In Niigata, farmers on the terraces are ageing and Tokamachi already recruits volunteers to keep them planted. We put the two together: you sponsor the field, the farmer tends it, and you come for a weekend, or two. The waiting list is how we get noticed. The reason people pay is the field, the sake and the craft.

The launch campaign: posters on the London Underground, Berlin U-Bahn and Paris Métro, and search ads on "allotment waiting list". Sources: The Guardian and National Allotment Society, 2023; Bundesverband Deutscher Gartenfreunde. Concept posters, AI imagery.

Niigata's winter is famous. Its summer is what the winter is for.
The Field Share

Your own piece of snow country, for a year.

The snow that brings skiers in February becomes the water that grows the rice in June. A Field Share lets you follow that water all the way into a glass.

Your plot

About 150 m² of terrace, marked on a map with your name.

One weekend, or both

Plant in June, harvest in October, or come for both. Each is two days, hosted in English.

Your own cup

Day two of harvest weekend: hammer a copper cup in Tsubame. It goes home with you.

Your field's sake

Six bottles from your terrace's rice, ready in February. Collect them or have them shipped.

A 12 million year old bath

After planting, float in Matsunoyama's onsen: seawater trapped underground 12 million years ago.

A glass you blow

Day two of planting weekend: blow your own glass at Tsukioka. It waits for you at harvest, or we ship it home.

¥65,000a year for two · one weekend
¥75,000a year for two · both weekends
Proposed prices
Already real, in Japanese. The Matsudai Tanada Bank in Tokamachi rents 150 m² terrace shares for ¥46,200 a year, with planting and harvest days, and a local brewery already brews with its rice. Tsubame's industrial museum runs the copper cup activity for up to 20 people a session. The Field Share joins them up and opens them to the world.

Leave a little room

Optional extras, planned separately.

The core weekends stay small and easy. These add colour if you have time.

Another craft

A colour that is yours.

At the same Tsubame museum, colour a titanium spoon or fork in one of 24 colours. Three to five minutes.

Museum activities ↗
Included on planting weekend

A glass of your own, and an emerald bath.

Planting weekend ends at Tsukioka. Blow a glass at the Biidoro workshop (about 20 minutes, ¥3,300). It cools overnight, so your host collects it and hands it to you at harvest. Stay longer and soak in one of Japan's most sulphurous springs. Check each inn's bath and tattoo policy.

About Tsukioka ↗
A summer ride

Ride the rice fields.

The Yukiguni Uonuma Golden Cycle Route runs through the rice fields of Yuzawa, Minamiuonuma and Uonuma. A good July or August return trip.

Green season ideas ↗
A Tsubame evening

Tetris after the cup.

Iris Bowl in Tsubame keeps over 20 classic table arcade machines, from Street Fighter II to the original Mario, from the owner's own collection. Hours and prices are not published; check before you go.

Retro arcades in Niigata ↗
A night in the city

Market, sake, old port.

Pier Bandai market for grilled seafood, Ponshukan's sake tasting by the station, and Furumachi's old geisha streets.

ANA's role

Every member flies in. The keenest fly twice.

A concept for how the airline could carry the Field Share end to end. Nothing here is an existing service or agreement.

Fly in, once or twice

London, Paris, Frankfurt and Munich to Haneda fares, timed to the planting and harvest weekends, with a return fare offer for the second weekend.

Miles for a field

Earn and spend ANA Mileage Club miles on a Field Share.

Pour it in the lounge

Terrace sake served in ANA lounges, with its field's story on a card.

Onward to Kansai

Niigata to Osaka Itami after each weekend, so the trip carries on west.

Measure it

Every member, trip and yen paid to a farmer is recorded: a live regional revitalisation case.

About this site

A concept for the Visit Japan 2026 Marketing Strategy Competition by a London Business School team. Nothing is bookable. Prices, plans and dates are proposals. Images and the film are AI generated concept scenes, not the real venues.
